clue.text: Destruction of Mac's clan - see gore in this event?

definitions.text: Destruction of Mac's clan - see gore in this event?

indicators.note: destroying something breaks it apart, so the following words are smashed and rebuilt in new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter, apostrophe dropped
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A grim note on the slaughter of a Scottish clan, inviting us to picture the bloodshed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the 1692 killing of the MacDonalds at Glencoe in the Scottish Highlands was a clan's destruction with gore aplenty.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1692 government troops slaughtered members of Clan MacDonald in their Highland glen, the most notorious killing in Scottish history.

clue.text: Bill's particular not to be seen? Bill's not this then!

definitions.text: Bill's particular not to be seen? Bill's not this then!

blocks.note: surface reading: a man called Bill is fussy

blocks.clueFragment: not to be seen? Bill's not this then!
blocks.note: setter's reading: an invoice broken down line by line, the opposite of a lump-sum bill that hides its details

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that fussy Bill dislikes being seen, then contradicts it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is an invoice, not a man; a bill set out item by item shows every particular, so one that keeps its details out of sight is not this.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice listing every charge separately is broken into individual entries, each particular shown on its own line.

clue.text: Make country journey north to see this lake

indicators.note: in a down entry north is upward, so one letter travels up the word and the order changes

blocks.note: the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: An invitation to travel north through the countryside to visit a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Make tells the solver to have a letter of EIRE move: the R climbs one place up the column, turning EIRE into ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erie is one of North America's five Great Lakes, bordered by Ontario and several American states.

clue.text: Iris is lifeless in such a setting

definitions.text: Iris is lifeless in such a setting

blocks.note: surface reading: a flower, or a woman named Iris, without vitality
setter's reading: the coloured ring of an eye painted on an artificial one, which cannot live

explanation.surface: A flower, or a woman called Iris, looks dull in some particular backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris is the part of the eye, not a flower or name; an artificial eye carries a painted iris that is literally lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthetic replacing a lost eye is made of glass or acrylic with a painted iris and pupil.

clue.text: One of the things I stand on brings expression of incredulity

definitions.text: One of the things I stand on

blocks.clueFragment: One of the things I stand on
blocks.note: first meaning: the speaker's own lower limb
second meaning: a scornful exclamation of disbelief

explanation.surface: Something underfoot prompts a cry of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a body part belonging to me; idiomatically a retort meaning 'nonsense!' when someone claims something unbelievable.

clue.text: Corresponding with friend, penning everything in red almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the colour word is dropped
to pen is to enclose, as in a sheep pen, so the friend wraps around what follows
one item sits inside the shortened colour word

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
all means everything

explanation.surface: A friend writing letters to someone while holding everything in red ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Two enclosures nest here: the shortened colour sits inside the friend, and everything sits inside the colour. 'Corresponding' suggests letter-writing, but it means matching.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel things run alongside and match each other, so they are analogous or equivalent in some respect.

clue.text: Army - something that's charged when given frontal support

indicators.note: frontal says the second item is placed in front, so it comes first in the joined result

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or a body
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: An army surges forward with backing from the front ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a military charge to match 'Army', but here it is electric.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers, and the word still means a large military force.

clue.text: You've feast set in motion with song and poem

indicators.note: setting things moving stirs them about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the archaic form of you
the contraction taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has got a party going with music and verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction must be split: the archaic pronoun for 'you' plus the 've, before the jumble of the remaining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats wrote this narrative poem in 1819 about a girl's ritual on the night before a saint's feast day.

clue.text: Not one of the earlier supporters in the side

blocks.note: the opposite of earlier
one of the supporters is an ally

explanation.surface: Someone describes a team member who joined the side recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The side' sounds like a sports team, but it means sideways: something placed laterally lies at the side.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes position or movement towards the flank, sideways rather than front or back.

clue.text: First character in public house wanting beer to begin with

indicators.note: the drink is wanted at the start, so it is placed in front

blocks.note: ale is a beer
PH is the map abbreviation for a public house

explanation.surface: A notable figure at the pub wants a beer before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person in the pub, but it is a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the opening letter of the Hebrew alphabet, equivalent in position to alpha in Greek.

clue.text: What you'd expect to find in maths book

definitions.text: What you'd expect to find in maths

blocks.clueFragment: What you'd expect to find in maths
blocks.note: first meaning: the figures that fill arithmetic
second meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament, after Genesis, Exodus and Leviticus

explanation.surface: A plain question about the contents of a maths textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both what fills a maths book and the name of a Bible book that counts the Israelites.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures fill arithmetic texts, and the fourth Old Testament book is named for the census of the Israelites it records.

clue.text: Consider drinking a litre in special glass

indicators.note: whatever drinks takes something inside itself, so one part swallows the other

blocks.note: to opine is to consider or hold an opinion
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about downing a litre from a fancy glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking' and 'glass' set a bar-room scene, but the glass is a material, not a tumbler.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a milky, semi-translucent glass resembling the gemstone opal, used for decorative vases and lamps.

clue.text: River dwelling for Cockney

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the aitch at the start of words, so that first letter goes

blocks.note: a house is a dwelling

explanation.surface: A Londoner's word for a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney, the East London accent, famously drops the H, so HOUSE becomes 'OUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English waterways share this name, the best known flowing through York to the Humber estuary.

clue.text: Steps involved in money for something needing a cure

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up within it, so one part goes inside

blocks.note: pence are small units of British money
a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Taking measures with cash to fund a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like measures taken, but it is the countryside stile.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague or deadly epidemic disease is an affliction that cries out for medical treatment.

clue.text: Shrub from which bee pursues mum

indicators.note: what pursues comes after, so the insect goes behind the parent

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a drone is a male bee

explanation.surface: A bush out of which a bee comes chasing after someone's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The madrone is an evergreen tree or shrub of western North America related to the strawberry tree.

clue.text: One putting everything away?

blocks.note: surface reading: a tidy person who stores all things in their place
setter's reading: eating anything at all, plant or animal

explanation.surface: A description of a tidy person who tucks every item into its place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting away' is slang for eating, so the tidy person becomes a creature that eats all kinds of food.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal with a diet of both plants and meat feeds on all kinds of food.

clue.text: New York hotel's bricked up, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the answer is a sound match

blocks.note: bricked up means sealed behind a wall

explanation.surface: A news item that a famous Manhattan hotel has been sealed off with bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'walled off' matches the hotel's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Waldorf Astoria is a famous luxury hotel on Park Avenue in Manhattan.

clue.text: One's bored, not having broken up - there's nothing jolly in that!

indicators.note: in that places the following items within the intact word just given

blocks.note: unbroken means whole
zero, shaped like the letter O
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A dull person, not yet divorced, complains there is no fun in married life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's bored' sounds like a weary person but means a tunnel drilled by a worm. Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunnel drilled by a burrowing grub through wood or fruit is literally a hole that has been bored.

clue.text: Part of the Establishment that gives you the blues

blocks.note: first meaning: the two ancient universities whose graduates fill Britain's ruling elite
second meaning: a blue is a sporting honour awarded by these two universities, dark and light blue

explanation.surface: A grumble that the ruling elite makes people miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue is a sporting honour given by the two oldest English universities, whose colours are dark and light blue; together they form part of the British Establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint name for Oxford and Cambridge universities, whose graduates dominate Britain's ruling elite.

clue.text: What Americans gave Bill - and Hilary (sic)?

blocks.note: first meaning: Bill Clinton was re-elected president in 1996
second meaning: Hilary is the name of the university session after Michaelmas at Oxford and in the law courts

explanation.surface: A question about what American voters granted Bill and Hillary Clinton.
explanation.walkthrough: (sic) flags the one-L spelling: not Clinton's wife Hillary but Hilary, the second of the three terms in the Oxford year (after Michaelmas, before Trinity).
explanation.definitionFit: Clinton was re-elected for another four years in office; Hilary is the university session that comes after the autumn one.

clue.text: You can get awful colic swallowing a fabric

indicators.note: to swallow is to take in, so one item goes inside the other
something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that bad stomach pains can come from eating cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain cotton cloth, originally imported from Calicut in India.

clue.text: Most of the people from the old country

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a race is a people

explanation.surface: A description of the bulk of a population from some former land.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region of the Balkans, home to a people who fought Greeks and Romans.

clue.text: A conjunction is used to make join

blocks.note: taken as written
but is a conjunction

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: conjunctions exist to connect things.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true of grammar, since conjunctions do join clauses, which hides that 'join' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoin share a border, touching end to end or side to side.

clue.text: A Romeo about 50 is completely done for

indicators.note: about means around, so the first part wraps the number

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Shakespeare's Romeo is the archetypal lover

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old ladies' man is washed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About 50' reads as an age, but it puts the Roman 50 inside A LOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is finished and there is no hope left, people say it is the end, totally ended.

clue.text: Fish gets front of hook, making mistake

indicators.note: front of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: its first letter
erring means going wrong

explanation.surface: A fish takes the hook by blundering.
explanation.definitionFit: A silvery North Atlantic food fish, sold smoked as kippers or pickled.

clue.text: Bar open to all, beginning to end

indicators.note: the opening letter is sent to the back of the word

blocks.note: free admission is open to all

explanation.surface: A pub welcomes everyone from opening till closing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but it is a ridge in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of rock, coral or sand lying near the surface of the sea is a sandbar or shoal.

clue.text: Winner in posh car, no slouch

indicators.note: in places the winner inside the vehicle

blocks.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, the archetypal luxury car
an ace is a winning serve in tennis

explanation.surface: A champion driving a luxury car proves to be quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is no slouch is fast, and a speedy runner, horse or car built for competition is one.

clue.text: Officer leading union is someone you can work with

indicators.note: leading means going first, so the officer comes before the union

blocks.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
a league is a union or alliance

explanation.surface: An officer heading a trade union is a good person to work alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A coworker shares your profession or workplace, a fellow member of staff.
